Show industry benchmarks.
For Lakeshore Holdings, industry benchmarks are not carried in the current business context — here is what the internal profile does reveal and why the gap matters.
• At $190.6M total IT spend against a $7.12B portfolio revenue rollup, Lakeshore Holdings's blended IT intensity sits at approximately 2.7% — a figure that reads lean for a diversified holding company managing four operating companies plus shared services, and warrants external calibration before any budget defense.
• The split between $36.5M corporate IT and $154.1M portfolio-local IT signals a decentralized operating model; peer benchmarks for holding companies typically flag this ratio as the first lever for consolidation value or governance risk, depending on where redundancy lives.
• Without an external benchmark anchor, the four active initiatives — ERP/HCM modernization, treasury visibility, contract lifecycle, and portfolio data foundation — cannot be sized against what comparable holding companies invest in equivalent transformation cycles.
Caveat: no third-party benchmark data is loaded in the current business context. External comparables require client-side sourcing or a validated peer data asset.
Branch: **Tower** to pressure-test IT spend ratios against value targets — **Intelligence** for holding-company peer benchmarks and consolidation tradeoff framing — **Source** if benchmark procurement or advisory contracts are in scope.
